text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- Yugoslav Supreme Defence Council decides to raise the degree of combat readiness of Yugoslav army in the region bordering with Albania.

- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic says the special ties agreement between Yugoslavia and Bosnian Serb Republic should have been first discussed in the Bosnian Serb parliament and said she would only sign such an agreement after it passed the required procedure.

- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic offers to go to Copenhagen on March 15 at the invitation of current OSCE chairman Niels Helve Petersen who proposed holding of separate talks between the Yugoslav government and the opposition coalition Zajedno there.
- The Belgrade University Council constituent session will be held on March 19, it is expected to endorse the resignation of rector Dragutin Velickovic.
- Five Yugoslav navy vessels are stationed off the Ulcinj coast because of the deteriorating situation in neighbouring Albania.

- New Democracy party is against privatisation of big state firms in the first round and for privatisation of medium and small firms first, because the current political situation considerably reduces the value of firms.
- Montenegrin government expected to adopt a privatisation plan on March 27 and to issue the first vouchers and launch ownership transformation in April.
- Partnership talks between Kragujevac Zastava and Korea's Hyundai are under way and results will be known soon, said the Korean charge d'affaires during visit to the Kragujevac car plant.
- The Yugoslav government will start issuing the first passports of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia on April 15 .
- The Serbian government has paid 54 percent of its total debt to the farmers for their last year's crops, says Serbian agriculture minister Jovan Babovic.
- Russian NTV and reporter Oleg Chupin demand 615,000 dinars in damages fom Serbian police for injuries sustained from police beatings during reporting at Belgrade rallies.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav government expresses concern with situation in Ablania and says it involves a deep destabilisation of the neighbouring country with implications for the stability of the region.

- Serbs have to be ready for elections and obtain necessary Croatian documents whether they plan to take part in them or not, said the head of the Serb government in Eastern Slavonia Vojislav Stanimirovic.
- Sanctions have had serious effects on Yugoslavia's energy sector and revival will take many years, it was concluded at an economists' round table on energy.

- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic says Yugoslav Bosnian Serb special ties agreement will contribute to stabilising peace during meeting with Serb member in Bosnian presidency Momciloo Krajisnik in Podgorica.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- New information bill does not have ideal solutions but is a good basis for making a good law through Serbia-wide discussions, it was concluded at a panel discussion in the Serbian parliament not attended by main opposition parties.

- If Yugoslavia continues to be a limiting factor of Montenegro's development its citizens have the right to opt to live independently according to the constitution, said Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic in Washington.
